catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class binds an oscilloscope (device_kind 'instrument') for an instrument-side scalar measurement: cap.sensing.read.v1 binds sensor, sensor.imu and sensor.force_torque, and cap.measure.voltage.v1 binds instrument.dmm, instrument.smu and sensor. The scope returns voltage, time and ratio items from ':MEASure:ITEM?', so the action uses an inline x-cap schema meanwhile.

notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed: no hardware backend was run and the wire syntax was not tried on an instrument. The command map uses the clone's literal SCPI commands (src/scopebench_mcp/drivers/rigol_dho.py); the hardware backend lets the SCPI bridge open host/port (default 5555, docs/compatibility_matrix.md:6) or a VISA resource, and this package does not import scopebench_mcp. The five numeric settings are Limit.operator_required because no text of the clone states their ranges (docs/development_plan.md:148-151); site-limits.example.json fills them with example bench bounds and may only narrow. NOT COVERED: the waveform array (:WAVeform:DATA?), the screen-image array (:DISPlay:DATA?), the memory-capture arrays, the statistics array, the pulse-width trigger, cursor measurements, autoscale, LAN configuration, screen capture and the synchronized multi-channel acquisition workflow. The driver exposes the clone's scalar instrument-side measurements (through the x-cap action and the CH1 state reads) and the CH1, timebase and trigger settings; channels 2-4 can be measured through the action, while the settings and the state reads are CH1 only. gate.digest is the digest the check printed (the check report without its clock); check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
